about: F2: discrete points 0..11, five-point arcs; no declared cut. This finite counterexample refutes pairwise sufficiency here, not every finite Helly bound.

coverage.why: finite arithmetic checks; not a general proof

complementSingleton.about: For every n>=3, the n arcs of n-1 consecutive cyclic points, each omitting a different point, have nonempty intersection for every proper subfamily and empty total intersection. Thus Helly numbers are unbounded across discrete circle sizes; each fixed n still has a bound <= n.
